items.rule: The nth term equals the difference of consecutive partial sums.
items.example: Subtract S_{n-1} from S_n after forming both expressions.

items.rule: For a finite AP with last term l, the nth term from the end is l-(n-1)d.
items.example: Move backward by n-1 common-difference steps.

items.example: For even N, use N/2 and N/2+1.

concepts.title: 1. Term-Sum Relationship
concepts.subtitle: a_n = S_n - S_{n-1}
concepts.summary: The nth term is the difference between the sums of the first n and first n-1 terms.
concepts.trap: Adding the sums or confusing S_n with a_n.

concepts.title: 2. nth Term from the End
concepts.subtitle: a'_n = l - (n - 1)d
concepts.summary: In a finite AP, move backward from the last term l by n-1 common-difference steps.
concepts.trap: Using + instead of - when moving backward.

concepts.title: 3. Middle Term(s)
concepts.subtitle: Locate the center of a finite AP
concepts.summary: For odd N, the middle position is (N+1)/2. For even N, the middle positions are N/2 and N/2+1.

points.text: Locate the middle index or pair.

concepts.trap: Using N/2 as the unique middle position when N is odd.

concepts.title: 4. Recovering a, d and a_k
concepts.subtitle: Read AP parameters from S_n
concepts.summary: Given a quadratic expression for S_n, compute S_n-S_{n-1} to recover the linear nth term, then compare with a+(n-1)d.
concepts.trap: Reading a and d directly from S_n without first finding a_n.

concepts.title: 5. Ratios of AP Terms from Sum Ratios
concepts.subtitle: Use n = 2m - 1
concepts.summary: The ratio of partial sums at n=2m-1 can be connected to the ratio of the corresponding m-th terms after substitution and simplification.

concepts.title: 6. Sum Identities
concepts.subtitle: Compare equivalent AP-sum forms
concepts.summary: Substitute n,2n,3n into the sum formula, simplify both sides, and show they match.
concepts.trap: Changing the outer n/2 factor incorrectly when replacing n by 2n or 3n.
